articles.title: How Tyson Fury overcame adversity to become heavyweight world champion
articles.summary: Inspired by his father John and drawn to boxing from a young age, Tyson Fury went on to become heavyweight world champion. BBC Sport takes a look at the defining moments that shaped one of Britain's most extraordinary sporting journeys.
articles.body:

articles.title: UFC CEO Dana White takes the White House podium during Washington visit
articles.summary: During his visit to meet with US President Donald Trump in Washington, Dana White answers questions at the White House.
articles.body:
UFC CEO Dana White takes the White House podium during Washington visit

During his visit to meet with US President Donald Trump in Washington, UFC CEO Dana White answers questions at the White House podium, joking about how his life in the last 24 hours ‘has been insane’ since Trump proposed White could be the new White House press secretary.

articles.title: UFC's Dana White Appears with Trump at a White House Briefing — But Won't Be His Press Secretary
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — After bringing UFC to the White House lawn this summer, President Donald Trump has now brought it to the briefing room, too.
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — After bringing UFC to the White House lawn this summer , President Donald Trump has now brought it to the briefing room, too.

Trump made a surprise appearance before reporters Monday with UFC chief Dana White and briefly stood aside as his longtime friend took questions — milking a joke that began over the weekend, when Trump said he had offered White the job of White House press secretary.

"I've always wanted to do this," White said, before bellowing, "Who has the first question?" He then clarified, "I have zero political aspirations."

The joke — and the briefing — were the latest in a series of unexpected choices by the president since Republicans' sweeping losses during last week's midterm elections . Trump's briefing room stop was so hastily organized that officials didn't have time to affix the presidential seal to the lectern from which he spoke.

The president had announced on social media Saturday that he wanted "the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior" as his next chief spokesman — catching White off-guard at a boxing match in London. "He called me and told me that he had done this," White said Monday. "The last 24 hours of my life has been insane."

Trump said he had been having a "very bad press day" and thought suggesting White as the 38th White House press secretary in the nation's history might be good for a laugh.

"We thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here," Trump said. "He would be fantastic."

White tells Trump, 'I do not want to be in politics, no.'

Some reporters in the press room played along. White was asked if he had any advice for Trump on the possibility of issuing a posthumous pardon for Pete Rose , baseball's all-time hits leader.

"I don't advise the president on anything ever," White responded. "But yeah, I think it's fair." Trump then interjected to say, "I'd give Pete Rose a pardon."

At one point, White marveled, "I can't believe you actually have questions for me."

Trump eventually took over. But after answering about half an hour of questions on the midterms, the war in Iran and a variety of serious topics, the president turned to White and asked, "Would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America" or "just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?"

"Thank you for the offer," White said, before allowing, "I do not want to be in politics, no."

Trump post-midterm moves have been peculiar

In the hours after Trump's Saturday post landed, neither the White House nor UFC would provide clarity on whether it was serious . Then, on Sunday night, Trump finally said, "I was kidding, but I think Dana likes the idea, and he is a very capable guy."

Trump has long relished doing the norm-busting unexpected as president, but he's leaned even more into that tendency around the election.

The day before balloting began, Trump used what was billed as a speech outlining his closing argument for why his party deserved to continue to control Congress to instead talk up his costly and problem-plagued effort to overhaul the Lincoln Memorial's Reflecting Pool.

On Wednesday, after Democrats won all over the country, including notching Senate seats in deep red states like Texas, South Carolina and Kansas, he took reporters on a tour of the White House ballroom's construction site and even signed a steel beam .

The following day, Trump declared the Oval Office would become a national monument — even though that won't prevent future presidents from undoing the gilded flourishes he's packed it with.

On Friday, the White House promoted a glitzy new website celebrating plans for a towering memorial arch in Trump's honor, despite a court order blocking work on it.

The White House press secretary position is open due to the brief, tumultuous week when Trump tried out Katie Zacharia as press secretary. She struggled in her sole appearance before reporters and left the job after five days.

The post had been vacant since Karoline Leavitt left at the end of August.

Trump has frequently attended UFC events with White. The pair have been friends for decades, and White spoke at the last three Republican National Conventions.

Trump even allowed White's sport to take over the White House's South Lawn in June for the celebration of America's 250th year of independence and the president's own 80th birthday. A wire-mesh Octagon was constructed under " The Claw ," a spaceship-like metal arch fitted with lights, sound equipment and large screens.

"He's really very unique," Trump said, describing his friend, in the White House briefing room. "The only problem is he'll talk for a little while and then he's going to beat the hell out of you."
authors: Will Weissert and Seung Min Kim, Associated Press

articles.title: From $600 Million Sale to Brand Fallout: The End of Conor McGregor's Whiskey Run
articles.summary: Conor McGregor's Irish whiskey shipped more than six million bottles before the sale closed.
articles.body:
Former two-division UFC champion Conor McGregor named his whiskey for the Dublin district where he grew up. Proper No. Twelve nods to Crumlin, in Dublin 12 .

Manager Audie Attar and Ken Austin, a Teremana Tequila co-founder, launched Proper No. Twelve with McGregor in September 2018 . Proximo makes it at the Old Bushmills Distillery in Northern Ireland.

The whiskey shipped more than 500,000 nine-liter cases across eight markets in under three years. Proximo said its Instagram account was the most followed in spirits.

Becle, the Jose Cuervo owner and Proximo's parent, already owned 49%, a stake it reached in May 2020. In April 2021, it bought the remaining 51%.

Proximo confirmed the deal was worth up to $600 million, including $250 million already paid to the founders.

Proximo president and CEO Mike Keyes weighed in on the sale.

"When we launched, the Irish whiskey market was dominated by one brand," Keyes said. "Now, Proper No. Twelve has disrupted the category and has become a leading brand in the industry."

Under the deal, McGregor kept an interest in the brand and remained its frontman.

"This agreement is exciting for my partners and me, and the potential is limitless," he said.

The sale reportedly brought him about $130 million .

That partnership ended in November 2024. A Dublin civil jury found him liable for sexually assaulting Nikita Hand at a hotel in December 2018.

"Since 2021, Proximo Spirits has been the 100% owner of Proper No. Twelve Irish Whiskey," the company said . It added that it would stop using his name and likeness in marketing.

Tesco and Musgrave, which runs SuperValu and Centra, pulled the whiskey from shelves.

McGregor, 38, lost to Max Holloway at UFC 329 in July after suffering a knee injury in the opening seconds. The fight was stopped at 1:09 of the first round.

While the bottle still carries the Dublin 12 likeness, its marketing no longer points to the UFC icon.

articles.title: Donald Trump jokes he's 'devastated' after Dana White rules out White House press secretary role
articles.summary: Following a bizarre weekend, Trump and White put the press secretary saga to rest with a joint briefing in the nation’s capital.
articles.body:
UFC CEO Dana White made his much-discussed visit to the White House on Monday, where he joined U.S. President Donald Trump for a press briefing and officially turned down the president's tongue-in-cheek offer to become his new press secretary.

Following a bizarre weekend in which Trump appeared to float the open role of White House press secretary to the UFC boss in a Truth Social post, only to admit a day later that he was "only kidding, but Dana loves the idea," Trump and White put the discussion to rest to close out a joint press briefing with the two in the nation's capital.

Trump: "So let me ask you the big question. Dana, would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America. Look at the sign — you'd have this behind all the time, 'The White House, Washington.' Would you like that or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?" White: "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics." Trump: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everyone."

Trump: "So let me ask you the big question. Dana, would you like to be press secretary of the United States of America. Look at the sign — you'd have this behind all the time, 'The White House, Washington.' Would you like that or do you just want to stay with this ridiculous UFC?"

White: "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics."

Trump: "I am devastated to hear this. Goodbye, everyone."

White briefly took questions from reporters during the press appearance, after which Trump explained how the peculiar situation first arose.

"We were having a very bad press day and I don't know why, I thought of his name," Trump said. "He's been a friend for a long time. I said, 'I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary.' I said it to a group of the press and that was it. I was sort of kidding.

"Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn't kidding, and then [White] was inundated and I was inundated. He was here anyway and we thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here. He would be fantastic."

"The last 24 hours of my life have been insane," White added.

White and Trump have maintained a close personal relationship for decades, dating back to the early days of the UFC's rise in the United States, when Trump's Atlantic City hotel and casino hosted two of the promotion's events in 2001. White has since become one of Trump's most prominent supporters in the sports world, speaking at three Republican National Conventions and publicly backing Trump's presidential campaigns.

White's initial reaction to Trump's social media post Saturday only further fueled speculation around his potential appointment. White first posted an image of himself at the podium of the White House press briefing room with the caption, "On to the next chapter," then told reporters in London that he was "flying to Washington" directly after Zuffa Boxing 12's post-fight press conference in order to meet with Trump on Monday.

Trump clarified Sunday that his meeting with White was previously scheduled and concerned unrelated matters, which both men reiterated Monday afternoon.

In the end, it appears the whole saga ended up being much ado about nothing.

articles.title: Dana White Turns Down Donald Trump’s Press Secretary Offer in Hilarious Exchange at White House
articles.summary: Dana White makes a surprise White House appearance alongside Donald Trump, turning down the President’s offer to become press secretary.
articles.body:
So, the real-life episode of The Office continues. Just two days after Donald Trump jokingly offered him the role of press secretary in his administration, Dana White made a personal appearance at the White House. For the unversed, the President had taken to his Truth Social account to announce that the UFC CEO and several other fighters were welcome to join his cabinet.

However, just a day after the announcement, Trump clarified that the offer was made in a jovial spirit and that he was only joking. While he maintained that White would be a fantastic choice for the position, he insisted that there was nothing serious behind the proposal.

The UFC CEO had confirmed that he would meet Trump on November 9 after returning to the United States from the Zuffa Boxing 12 event in London. However, the President later clarified that White's visit had nothing to do with the press secretary offer. According to Trump, the UFC boss was already planning to be in Washington and had simply decided to stop by and see him.

And that is exactly what White ended up doing. During the November 9 White House news conference alongside Trump, White officially turned down the prospect of becoming press secretary.

While admitting that he doesn't say no to the President, the UFC CEO made it clear that he had no interest in entering politics at the moment. He said, "I don't tell the president no to anything. I didn't say no. Literally every media outlet was calling me, and I didn't want to be disrespectful and say anything until he said something first."

Trump then added to the bizarre nature of the situation by reiterating that he had been joking about the entire proposition. He said, "We were having a very bad press day, and I don't know why, I thought of his name; he's been a friend for a long time. I said I think I'm going to get Dana White to be my new press secretary. I said it to a group of the press, and that was it. I was sort of kidding."

The President further explained, "Then they wrote the stories as though I wasn't kidding, and then [Dana] was inundated and I was inundated. He was here anyway, and we thought we'd have a little fun and we brought Dana here. He would be fantastic."

White's rejection then became the subject of another lighthearted exchange when Trump jokingly asked him whether he would leave " the ridiculous UFC " to accept the position in his administration. White responded, "Thank you for the offer, sir. I do not want to be in politics."

Keeping the laughter-filled atmosphere going, Trump claimed he was "devastated" by White's response before bringing the briefing to a close.

articles.title: Canelo Álvarez busca revanchas con Terence Crawford y Dmitry Bivol
articles.standfirst: "Ojalá y Crawford vuelva del retiro, porque es una revancha a la que apuntamos o una revancha con Bivol, aunque ya veremos qué viene el año que entra"
articles.summary: "Ojalá y Crawford vuelva del retiro, porque es una revancha a la que apuntamos o una revancha con Bivol, aunque ya veremos qué viene el año que entra"
articles.body: Eddy Reynoso, entrenador del mexicano Saúl 'Canelo' Álvarez, afirmó que el boxeador buscará tener peleas de revancha con el estadounidense Terence Crawford, hoy en retiro, y el ruso Dmitry Bivol. "Ojalá y Crawford vuelva del retiro, porque es una revancha a la que apuntamos o una revancha con Bivol, aunque ya veremos qué viene el año que entra. Están esas posibilidades, también me gusta Iglesias; vamos a ver", afirmó Reynoso. El entrenador del 'Canelo' habló durante la inauguración sexagésima cuarta convención del Consejo Mundial de Boxeo (CMB), que preside Mauricio Sulaimán. "Estamos contentos con el regreso que Saúl tuvo luego de la derrota con Crawford, regresamos después de un año, Saúl venció a Mbilli, hizo un gran trabajo con lo que se volvió a coronar y eso nos tiene satisfechos, ahora debemos preparar el calendario del próximo año con la gente de Arabia para intentar pelear en marzo o mayo", señaló Eddy. El 31 de octubre pasado, 'el Canelo' derrotó por decisión unánime a Christian Mbilli, en Arabia, para obtener el cinturón de campeón mundial de peso supermediano del CMB. El entrenador del pugilista mexicano reconoció que Álvarez quedó dolido por las derrotas ante Bivol y Crawford, dos de los tres descalabros que suma en su carrera, por lo que una de las prioridades es conseguir revanchas, aunque para ello deben sacar a Terence Crawford del retiro. "A mí me gusta mucho la posibilidad de una revancha con Crawford, es la que vamos a buscar, o como ya dije, con Bivol; también está Iglesias, y si no, alguna pelea de unificación del título", reiteró el entrenador. Reynoso se refirió al cubano Osleys Iglesias, campeón supermediano de la Federación Internacional de Boxeo, para una contienda que unifique el título. Eddy Reynoso también aseguró que están adelantados para alargar el contrato que tiene 'el Canelo' con Turki Al-Sheikh, presidente de la autoridad general de entretenimiento de Arabia Saudí. "Vamos a renovar, hay muy buenos planes para Saúl, ya lo habló con Turki y hay buenos planes para seguir la carrera", concluyó el entrenador.

articles.title: Denzel Bentley: 'I'd happily go to Ireland, beat Aaron McKenna in his home town and bring the belt back to England'
articles.summary: After Saturday's victory over Shane Mosley Jr, Denzel Bentley is looking to become a world champion once again as he targets Carlos Adames or Aaron McKenna; Watch Carlos Adames fight Gerome Warburton this Saturday live on Sky Sports.
articles.body:
Bentley was the WBO middleweight champion only to be stripped of the belt for boxing Mosley Jr, a world-rated contender, rather than fighting mandatory challenger Yoenli Hernandez immediately.

Bentley dropped Mosley Jr with a stunning knockdown in the second round and ultimately secured a unanimous decision win in London.

He is now targeting IBF champion Aaron McKenna and WBC titlist Carlos Adames. McKenna is an appealing fight for Bentley, who is willing to travel to Ireland to make it happen.

"He's a champion. When I was a champion and we were trying to make that happen, [I thought] no, I want to bring it home, I can have a bit of pulling power," Bentley told Sky Sports .

Now, Bentley points out: "He's a champion. He wants it at home and I want an opportunity at his belt, what he obtained and what he wants to defend, who am I to say no?

"I'd happily go to Ireland, beat him in his home town and then bring it back to England and defend it in my hometown."

Discussions for Bentley to fight McKenna have been held before. McKenna's manager Mike Borao told Sky Sports : "Aaron wanted to unify the titles with Bentley this year, unfortunately the request was denied by the WBO. In any event, I believe McKenna vs Bentley is a strong possibility for next year."

Bentley noted: "They were up for it, I was up for it.

"There's a bit of history. Not animosity but a bit of history because there's been links to it, talks about it. There was potential of it happening. I think that would be the obvious one to make.

"He'd have the whole of Ireland behind him, I'd have part of England that's not angry at me right now supporting me, it would just all be good. It would just make a great fight.

"That's what I'm about, I want to be in great fights, great, big fights."

articles.title: Boxing: Vote for your greatest all-British boxing fight
articles.summary: From bitter rivalries and controversial decisions to dramatic knockouts, we look back at five unforgettable all-British boxing contests and ask you to vote for the greatest.
articles.body:
From bitter rivalries to controversial decisions and dramatic knockouts, British boxing has produced some unforgettable nights.

But which all-British fight staged on home soil stands above the rest?

With Tyson Fury v Anthony Joshua just over a month away, Stacey Copeland will be joined by 5 Live boxing pundit Steve Bunce and esteemed boxing commentator Mike Costello on BBC Radio 5 Live at 19:30 GMT on Wednesday, 11 November to debate five of the greatest domestic contests.

Take a look at the five fights below and let us know which deserves top spot.

Have your say in our vote, which closes at 12:00 GMT on 11 November, at the bottom of the page. The results will be revealed during Wednesday's show.

It was the end of an era when 21-year-old Joe Bugner faced British boxing favourite Henry Cooper at Wembley's Empire Pool. Cooper, affectionately known as 'Our 'Enry', was 36 and defending his British, European and Commonwealth heavyweight titles against a man 15 years his junior.

After 15 gruelling rounds, Bugner claimed a hugely controversial points victory by just a quarter of a point. The decision was met with boos from the crowd, while BBC commentator Harry Carpenter protested: "How can you take the man's three titles away like that?"

Cooper announced his retirement afterwards, with the result remaining one of the most fiercely debated in British boxing history.

Nigel Benn v Chris Eubank - November 1990

Few rivalries have captured the British public's imagination quite like Nigel Benn and Chris Eubank. The aggressive, hard-hitting Benn and flamboyant, outspoken Eubank were contrasting characters who shared a genuine dislike for one another.

Their first meeting at Birmingham's NEC lived up to the bitter build-up, with the pair trading punishing blows in a ferocious contest.

Benn was ahead on two scorecards when Eubank forced a dramatic ninth-round stoppage to claim the WBO middleweight title. The result launched one of British boxing's defining rivalries, with their 1993 rematch at Old Trafford ending in a draw.

Lennox Lewis v Frank Bruno - October 1993

It was a clash between two of Britain's biggest heavyweight stars, but Lennox Lewis and Frank Bruno arrived in Cardiff with contrasting reputations.

Bruno was a hugely popular figure still chasing his first world title, while Lewis, born in London but raised in Canada, was defending his WBC heavyweight crown.

Bruno made the stronger start and was ahead on one scorecard, with the other two level, before Lewis turned the contest around with a devastating left hook and a flurry of punches in the seventh round.

The victory cemented Lewis' status as world champion, while Bruno would have to wait another two years to finally fulfil his world title dream.

Carl Froch v George Groves - November 2013

Bad blood between Carl Froch and George Groves produced a sensational world super-middleweight title fight in Manchester, with the younger challenger determined to prove he belonged at the highest level.

Groves stunned the champion with a first-round knockdown and was ahead on all three scorecards before Froch fought back.

But referee Howard Foster's decision to stop the contest in the ninth round sparked outrage, with sections of the crowd booing and Groves insisting he had been robbed of victory.

The controversy only intensified their rivalry, setting up a blockbuster rematch at Wembley in front of 80,000 fans six months later.

Fabio Wardley v Daniel Dubois - May 2026

The most recent fight on the list was a remarkable display of heavyweight resilience at Manchester's Co-op Live arena.

Fabio Wardley, whose rise from white-collar boxing to world champion had captured the imagination, floored Daniel Dubois just 10 seconds into their WBO title contest and again in the third round.

But Dubois, whose determination had been questioned after previous defeats, produced an extraordinary comeback, repeatedly hurting a bloodied Wardley before forcing an 11th-round stoppage.

Promoter Frank Warren described it as the best heavyweight fight he had ever put on. The pair met again five months later, with Dubois winning a far more one-sided rematch in the second round.

articles.title: Trump está "desolado" por las calabazas de Dana White para ser portavoz de Casa Blanca: "No quiero"
articles.standfirst: "Tengo cero aspiraciones políticas... Gracias por el ofrecimiento, señor. No quiero dedicarme a la política"
articles.summary: "Tengo cero aspiraciones políticas... Gracias por el ofrecimiento, señor. No quiero dedicarme a la política"
articles.body: El director ejecutivo de la UFC, Dana White, la principal organización de artes marciales mixtas del mundo, que fue tanteado por el presidente Donald Trump para ser portavoz de la Casa Blanca, apareció este lunes en la sala de prensa de la residencia y rechazó el puesto: "Tengo cero aspiraciones políticas". "Gracias por el ofrecimiento, señor. No quiero dedicarme a la política", declaró White en la sala de prensa de la Casa Blanca. "Me deja desolado oír esto. Adiós a todos", respondió Trump en una aparición convocada en el último minuto la tarde del lunes. Previamente, Trump anunció en su red social Truth Social que había ofrecido el puesto de secretario de Prensa a "White, un luchador y guerrero implacable". En su mensaje, Trump explicó que le ha pedido que lleve a la Casa Blanca como asistentes a varios peleadores, aunque no sean estadounidenses, como Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier, Amanda Nunes y Kayla Harris. "Necesitamos a estas personas para defendernos de la izquierda lunática. Dana será un secretario de prensa como ningún otro. ¡Dana, por favor, acepta el puesto!", dijo. El puesto de portavoz de la Casa Blanca permanece vacante desde el pasado 16 de octubre, cuando Katie Zacharia fue cesada apenas cinco días después de asumir el cargo por su mal desempeño, convirtiéndose en la persona que menos tiempo lo ha desempeñado. Las elecciones de medio mandato del pasado martes, que se interpretaron como un referéndum sobre la gestión de Trump, se saldaron con una rotunda victoria de la oposición demócrata, que arrebató a los republicanos el control de ambas cámaras del Congreso.

articles.title: UFC 334: Ciryl Gane v Josh Hokit and Kayla Harrison v Amanda Nunes - all you need to know
articles.summary: All you need to know as Ciryl Gane defends his heavyweight title against Josh Hokit and Kayla Harrison puts her women's bantamweight belt on the line against Amanda Nunes.
articles.body:
Ciryl Gane will make the first defence of his heavyweight title against Josh Hokit at UFC 334 in New York on Saturday.

The Frenchman was promoted to undisputed champion in September after Britain's Tom Aspinall vacated the belt because of complications in recovering from an eye injury.

The co-main event at Madison Square Garden features the return of UFC legend Amanda Nunes, who faces Kayla Harrison for the bantamweight title.

The fight was originally set to take place in January but was postponed after American champion Harrison suffered a neck injury.

Britain's Chris Duncan is also in action, with the 33-year-old Scotsman taking on American lightweight Drew Dober on the prelims.

Everything you need to know about UFC 334 is below.

The main card is expected to start at 02:00 GMT, with the headline fight between Gane and Hokit likely to take place at around 04:30 GMT on Sunday.

Ciryl Gane v Josh Hokit (UFC world heavyweight title)

Kayla Harrison v Amanda Nunes (UFC women's bantamweight world title)

Caio Borralho v Yousri Belgaroui (middleweight)

Uros Medic v Kevin Holland (welterweight)

Stephen Thompson v Charles Radtke (welterweight)

Jim Miller v Terrance McKinney (lightweight)

Donte Johnson v Cesar Almeida (middleweight)

All you need to know about Gane and Hokit

Gane beat Alex Pereira for the interim heavyweight title at the UFC's White House event in June.

That bout was set up while former champion Aspinall was unable to compete after suffering an eye injury at the hands of Gane in October 2025 in a bout deemed a no-contest.

The UFC's plan was for a rematch between Aspinall and Gane for the undisputed title, but with the Briton still unable to compete, he vacated the belt with Gane being upgraded from interim champion.

It marked the first time Gane, 36, has held the undisputed belt after losing in title fights against Francis Ngannou in 2022 and Jon Jones in 2023.

Gane debuted in 2018 and has won 14 of his 17 fights while securing seven knockouts.

American Hokit is fifth in the UFC heavyweight rankings and is fighting for the title after only one year in the organisation.

The 28-year-old debuted in the UFC last November and has won all four fights since, with his last win coming against Derrick Lewis in June.

In a similar vein to Colby Covington, Hokit adopts various controversial personas and characters during interviews to generate attention from fans.

He has been accused of overstepping the line into discrimination, however, after making racially aggravating and misogynistic comments in his post UFC 324 interview in January.

After Hokit directed misogynistic comments towards former First Lady Michelle Obama in June, UFC president Dana White described his words as "gross", "moronic", and "inappropriate".

Former NFL player Hokit is unbeaten since his MMA debut in 2023, winning all 10 fights with six of his wins coming via knockout.

Gane is the pre-fight favourite to beat Hokit and retain his heavyweight title.

All you need to know about Harrison and Nunes

The contest between Harrison and Nunes is being described by pundits as one of the biggest women's fights in UFC history.

The pair are friends and former team-mates at American Top Team Gym, before Brazil's Nunes left in 2022.

Nunes, 38, is widely regarded as the best women's MMA fighter of all time.

The former featherweight and bantamweight champion is the only woman in history to hold two UFC titles in two weight classes simultaneously.

She retired in 2023, bringing her glittering 15-year career to a close after winning 23 of her 28 fights, with 13 wins coming via knockout.

Nunes' bout against Harrison will be her first since she defended the UFC bantamweight title against Irene Aldana in 2023, before later retiring and vacating the belt.

Harrison won the title off Julianna Pena last year and is making the first defence of her belt.

The 36-year-old is a former two-time PFL lightweight world champion, before claiming gold in the UFC in only her third fight in the promotion.

Overall, Harrison has won 19 of her 20 fights with her only defeat coming against Larissa Pacheco in 2022.

Nunes holds a number of UFC records at bantamweight, including the most wins (13), finishes (eight) and longest win streak (nine).

Harrison is the pre-fight favourite to beat Nunes and retain her bantamweight title.

articles.summary: El público interpretó que se le dirigía un gesto obsceno
articles.body: El boxeador francés Murad Aliev se salvó de ser linchado tras un combate en Estambul contra el turco Umut Camkiran correspondiente al título del peso pesado CMB de categoría plata. El púgil francés, de origen azerí y que fue presentado en los prolegómenos del combate como azerbaiyano, realizó presuntamente un gesto obsceno que dio origen a un tumulto en el que fue incluso golpeado por su propio rival, pero ya tras el combate. Aliyev, presuntamente, se tocó la parte inferior del abdomen, si bien él señaló que estaba señalándole al árbitro que había recibido un golpe bajo. El gesto fue interpretado sin embargo por el público y el rival como provocación y dio origen al incidente. Decenas de espectadores saltaron al ring y golpearon también, con puños y sillas, a Aliev. Según informa L'Equipe, la seguridad del recinto no impidió la invasión del ring ni tampoco protegió a Aliev cuando huía hacia los vestuarios recibiendo golpes. Finalmente, consiguió ponerse a salvo. Aliev fue, por cierto, proclamado vencedor pero ya en los vestuarios, ya que fue imposible hacerlo sobre el ring. El púgil fue olímpico por Francia en Tokio 2020 y allí protagonizó un curioso incidente: descalificado durante su combate contra el británico Frazer Clarke, se negó a abandonar el ring y estuvo allí una hora sentado. Parte de la explicación del incidente puede deberse también al hecho de que Aliev fue presentado como azerbaiyano en un contexto de relaciones tirantes entre ambos países. El gobierno azerí ha publicado diversas leyes en pro del laicismo en los últimos meses -sobre todo una relativa a la prohibición del velo islámico en las escuelas-, contestadas por la población islamista conservadora de Turquía, donde gobierna aunque en minoría el islamista Erdogan. Sin embargo, un día después de estos incidentes los presidentes de ambos países se reunieron para mitigar tensiones, si bien no fue este combate el motivo directo del encuentro. El presidente azerí se llama, por cierto, Ilham Aliyev.

articles.title: Oleksandr Usyk could be tempted to stay at heavyweight for a trilogy fight with Tyson Fury, says promoter Frank Warren
articles.summary: If Tyson Fury beats Anthony Joshua in December, Oleksandr Usyk could be tempted to stay at heavyweight for a trilogy fight with Fury, says promoter Frank Warren; Usyk is considering moving down to cruiserweight, with David Benavidez a potential target; Usyk last boxed at cruiser in 2018
articles.body:
Usyk has an outstanding legacy at heavyweight, having previously beaten Fury twice and twice become the undisputed champion of the division without losing a fight.

But he has previously also been an undisputed champion at cruiserweight and his team have revealed that he could return to his old weight class , where star names like David Benavidez and Jai Opetaia could become targets.

Fury though is eager to box Usyk for a third time and if he beats Anthony Joshua in their December mega-fight, that may nevertheless still be a more appealing option for Usyk than the potential fight with Benavidez.

"I would have thought so," Frank Warren, Fury's promoter, told Sky Sports .

Usyk does have options at heavyweight, as far as Warren is concerned. Warren also promotes WBC champion Agit Kabayel, new IBF titlist Filip Hrgovic and Moses Itauma.

Usyk, if he wished to, could fight "all of them" believes Warren. Kabayel, the popular German who defends against Nelson Hysa on November 28, could fill a stadium in Europe against Usyk.

Warren suggested as well for Usyk: "Him and Hrgovic, loads of fights, him and Moses, if Moses comes back. There are some fabulous fights to be made there. Him and Tyson, if Tyson comes through. Irrespective of the results, they were good fights to watch. They were exciting fights."

The 39-year-old Usyk has been boxing at heavyweight since 2019. Moving back down in weight after all that time - he could have to lose between 20lb-30lb - especially at this late stage of his career will be a physical challenge even for the brilliant Ukrainian.

The decision to go back to cruiserweight was unexpected. "I'm very surprised about that. It's very difficult as well to lose weight as you get older," Warren said.

"It's very difficult. It's not like he didn't look solid. He looked quite solid. He's got to shift some timber now to get down to that weight.

"I like Alex, I think he's been a great champion at heavyweight and to go back down again, it's going to be interesting to see what he looks like and how comfortable he makes the weight.

"He vacated the belts he didn't do his mandatories. We'll see. He's done everything that's been asked of him, maybe for him it's a smart move. We will see. Time will tell."

articles.title: UFC veteran slams Jake Hager for Power Slap: ‘This is the dumbest thing’
articles.summary: Earlier this year, after finishing up his WWE and AEW career, former pro-wrestler Jake Hager signed up with Dana White’s Power Slap. However, the decision ha...
articles.body:
Earlier this year, after finishing up his WWE and AEW career, former pro-wrestler Jake Hager signed up with Dana White's Power Slap. However, the decision has turned out to be extremely costly for Hager. The former WWE Superstar has participated in three Power Slap fights, where he has already lost two.

Following his debut win over Devin Jenkins, he suffered a loss to Amanpreet Singh. Hager then suffered another brutal loss to Johnny Magna. Unfortunately, not only did Hager lose to Magna, but he also suffered a serious eye injury that required two surgeries, including one for a detached retina.

After Magna hit Hager in the face, blood started oozing out of Hager's eye. The scary moment soon went viral on the internet. Now, former UFC Heavyweight Champion Josh Barnett appeared on The Ariel Helwani Show, where he openly bashed the show as well as criticized Hager's decision to take part in it.

"It's the dumbest thing I've ever seen in my entire life. We've had our differences in the past, but watching Jake Hager go out there, it's just like, what are you doing? What are you thinking?

"It's the dumbest thing you could ever do. It kills me to see an Oklahoma wrestler, a collegiate D1 wrestler, an All-American, who wrestled in WWE and AEW and fought in Bellator, out there doing this. There's so much more you could do with your life and career. You'd be better off doing MMA than ever doing slap fighting… I can't say anything good about slap fighting," Barnett said.

Hager is still recovering from his two surgeries, and as of now, there are no confirmed return updates on him.

articles.title: McGregor está de vuelta: volcánica rueda de prensa y ataque a Max Holloway
articles.standfirst: El peleador irlandés criticó duramente a su último oponente en la UFC tras el evento de BKFC y habló de su recuperación tras sufrir una grave lesión de rodilla
articles.summary: El peleador irlandés criticó duramente a su último oponente en la UFC tras el evento de BKFC y habló de su recuperación tras sufrir una grave lesión de rodilla
articles.body: Este pasado fin de semana Conor McGregor volvió a ser el Conor McGregor que todos conocen. Tras un evento de BKFC, el peleador irlandés dio puro show en una rueda de prensa muy particular en la que se abrió una cerveza y criticó duramente a Max Holloway, su último oponente en el UFC 329 del pasado julio. Además, habló de cómo lleva la recuperación de su rotura de ligamento cruzado y cuándo piensa volver a pelear para acabar su contrato con la compañía. McGregor está decidido a que su última pelea en la UFC sea contra Max Holloway para cerrar su trilogía después de lesionarse a los tres segundos la última vez que se vieron las caras. De hecho, ha criticado duramente la actitud del peleador hawaiano, y ha vuelto a calentar el beef entre ambos para incentivar ese tercer duelo entre ambos. "El tipo no se involucró ni una sola vez. Él fue el que pidió la detención, yo habría peleado con una sola pierna. Holloway puede que sea un idiota, algo podría pasar. Pero un peleador que me enfrenta... ponle respeto a mi nombre. Si no eres campeón mundial, ni siquiera pronuncies mi maldito nombre. Si no has hecho una mierda pero tienes pocos likes, vete a la mierda", afirmó en la rueda de prensa. Según ha revelado en otras ocasiones, el objetivo de McGregor es recuperarse al 100% de su lesión e intentar regresar en la International Fight Week de verano de 2027 para poder tener la despedida que se merece de la UFC. Además, ha desvelado que todavía sigue asimilando lo que le ocurrió en su última aparición, y se niega a decir adiós de esa manera. "No voy a retirarme así. Voy a salir violentamente, con ferocidad, en un resplandor de gloria, de una forma u otra. Aún estoy jodidamente lidiando con ello. Estoy camino del regreso", finalizó. Lo que está claro es que los últimos años de la carrera de 'The Notorious' no hacen justicia a lo que ha hecho por el deporte, ya que es la mayor superestrella de la historia de las MMA y el tipo que lo cambió todo. Sin embargo, durante casi una década ha sido más noticia por sus escándalos que por sus combates, y en sus últimas dos peleas ha sufrido dos graves lesiones que le acompañarán de por vida.

articles.title: Cheavon Clarke 'should be on the shortlist for British fighter of the year' after Chris Billam-Smith knockout victory
articles.summary: Cheavon Clarke upset expectations to take out both Jack Massey and former world champion Chris Billam-Smith this year; Billam-Smith had never been dropped or stopped before; Watch Carlos Adames vs Gerome Warburton from 4pm live on Sky Sports Mix on Saturday
articles.body:
Clarke went into both of those fights perceived as the underdog and won both by stoppage.

Billam-Smith, renowned for his toughness, had never been knocked down before. He'd never even been dropped before.

But Clarke put him down twice, heavily, and hammered him to an inside-the-distance defeat.

He's in the kind of form that should make him a candidate for British boxer of the year.

"He definitely should be [on the shortlist] and hopefully next year he could maybe get a world title and be the UK fighter of the year," Dan Azeez, a former European champion, told Sky Sports .

"He had two back to back losses and then he's come back, beat Jack Massey in a stoppage, got off the canvas to win, and now he's just beat Chris Billam-Smith.

"He's just come and destroyed him in excellent fashion," Azeez added. "Those are the kind of stories that inspire people."

Britain has strong contenders for boxer of the year, not least Daniel Dubois becoming a two-time heavyweight world champion.

"It has to be Daniel Dubois, if I'm being honest," Azeez said, adding other contenders: "Willie Hutchinson WBC light-heavyweight champion… Ellie Scotney [who went undisputed].

"Chev, he could be," he continued. "He's definitely in the mix, he's done very well this year and my guy Denzel Bentley [who became world champion and beat Shane Mosley Jr]."

Former world champion George Groves told Sky Sports : "He's had a great year." Though Dubois would be his overall pick too.

"When you talk about Willie Hutchinson winning a world title this year, Daniel Dubois - two Wardley fights. Probably Dubois. To get off the floor in the first fight and look so spectacular in the second fight," he noted.

Clarke though deserves full credit for his performance against a former world champion in Billam-Smith.

"A great win for him," Groves said. "He had a plan, he stuck to it and found that shot that no one's found so far who's fought Chris Billam-Smith. It was a great, great performance from him."

It was an expert finish. "He stayed on him, didn't get reckless," Groves said. "Chris Billam-Smith's got fantastic powers of recovery, can weather a storm, can fight tired, can fight buzzed and still be effective so good for him."

It probably a merits a fight with someone like Jai Opetaia, widely regarded as the best fighter in the division. But Opetaia has a heavyweight bout against Deontay Wilder in December and won't be available to box for some time.

What should Clarke do next? "Does that feel like a step down if he fights [Ryan] Rozicki or [Brandon] Glanton? It would be a good fight," Groves said.

"Maybe Chris Billam-Smith will campaign for a rematch but maybe that's not the best thing for him right now.

"Chev's got the world at his feet in many ways now."

articles.title: Makhachev vuelve a hablar de su retirada: "Mi madre siempre ha opuesto a que pelee"
articles.standfirst: El campeón de peso wélter y mejor amigo de Khabib Nurmagomedov ha vuelto a dejar caer que le queda poco para colgar las guantillas
articles.summary: El campeón de peso wélter y mejor amigo de Khabib Nurmagomedov ha vuelto a dejar caer que le queda poco para colgar las guantillas
articles.body: Islam Makhachev es uno de los mejores peleadores de la historia de la UFC. El mejor amigo de Khabib Nurmagomedov cogió el testigo de 'The Eagle' en el peso ligero y batió el récord histórico de defensas de cinturón, para luego subir a peso wélter y convertirse en doble campeón, además de defender el título en otra ocasión. Sin embargo, a sus 35 años sabe que le quedan pocas peleas en su carrera, y en una reciente entrevista ha desvelado que su madre le está presionando para que se retire y pronto le hará caso. Los peleadores daguestaníes siempre han sido muy familiares, y se han dejado guiar por los consejos de sus progenitores. De hecho, Abdulmanap Nurmagomedov -padre de Khabib- fue el pionero de toda una camada de peleadores en Daguestán, y no hay que olvidar que 'The Eagle' decidió retirarse estando en su mejor momento después de su fallecimiento en la época del Covid-19. Le prometió a su madre que no pelearía sin su padre en la esquina, y eso hizo aunque a muchos les sorprendiese. Makhachev siempre le ha agradecido todo lo que tiene a la familia Nurmagomedov, y el propio Khabib le ha aconsejado no realizar muchas peleas más. Esto, sumado a los consejos de su madre, pueden ser un punto clave para Islam. "Mi madre siempre se ha opuesto a que pelee. Siempre he hecho caso a mi madre, así que pronto obedeceré su voluntad", reconoció en una entrevista con 'Red Corner MMA'. Lo cierto es que hay muy pocos retos que le queden pendientes a Makhachev como profesional, ya que su último logro fue superar a Anderson Silva y marcar el nuevo récord de más victorias consecutivas dentro de la UFC, después de su defensa del cinturón de peso wélter el pasado agosto ante Ian Garry. Doble campeón, número uno libra por libra, superestrella mundial... De hecho, muchos ya están empezando a meter a Makhachev en la conversación del GOAT de las MMA, y si consigue una o dos defensas más podría igualar a otros peleadores como Jon Jones o Georges St-Pierre en ese status. "No hay muchas cosas que puedan motivarme en este deporte. Estoy en la recta final. Solo quiero enfrentarme a los aspirantes al título, pero no veo nombres nuevos", finalizó. Se espera que a mediados de 2027 Makhachev se mida al ganador del duelo entre Carlos Prates y Michael Morales para unificar cinturones, y quién sabe si ese será su último combate profesional.

articles.title: Burned-out Amanda Nunes feared losing if she kept fighting — ‘I wasn’t happy’ | UFC 334
articles.summary: “The Lioness” is refreshed. Former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) champion and consensus women’s mixed martial arts (MMA) “GOAT” Amanda Nu...
articles.body:
Former two-division Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) champion and consensus women's mixed martial arts (MMA) "GOAT" Amanda Nunes returns to challenge former teammate Kayla Harrison for the Bantamweight title in UFC 334's co-main event this weekend (Sat., Nov. 14, 2026) inside iconic Madison Square Garden in New York City.

Nunes has not competed since her dominant title defense over Irene Aldana at UFC 289 in June 2023. Moments after the decision was announced, "The Lioness" placed both of her championship belts on the canvas and abruptly retired .

Several factors contributed to the decision.

Nunes wanted to spend more time with her growing family , had dealt with lingering nerve damage from years of fighting and had already accomplished virtually everything possible inside the Octagon.

The 38-year-old Brazilian also desperately needed to rest her mind.

"I feel amazing. I'm really happy to be back," Nunes told UFC.com. "I missed this. I missed everything about MMA. This has been in my life since I was a teenager. When I stepped out, I needed the rest because I was literally on a roll, fighting for so long — defended the belt in two divisions, and I never stopped. I was burned out."

Continuing to fight while mentally exhausted, Nunes believed, could have jeopardized both her legacy and her love for the sport.

"I didn't want to keep pushing through back then and have the risk to lose because I wasn't happy doing the thing that I love to do," Nunes added. "So, when I retired, I needed the break. I needed to reset and needed a clear mind. I needed a break for my body to lose weight, too."

"But when I got the break that I needed, it got boring," Nunes continued. "I got bored at home. My daughter got bored, and my little one didn't get the opportunity to see everything."

It just so happened that Harrison finally arrived in UFC during Nunes' retirement and quickly captured the championship her former American Top Team training partner once held.

Harrison's rise provided Nunes with the perfect challenge—and plenty of motivation to return.

The former teammates were originally scheduled to collide at UFC 324 in January. However, Harrison suffered a neck injury that required surgery , postponing the long-awaited title fight. Rather than compete against a replacement opponent for an interim belt, Nunes elected to wait for the champion to recover .

Now, barring another last-minute cancellation, Nunes will finally get the opportunity to put her hands on Harrison and attempt to become the first three-time UFC women's Bantamweight champion.

More importantly, she will enter the Octagon with the clear mind and renewed enthusiasm she was missing when she walked away three years ago.

articles.title: Inside TKO's Saudi Arabia crisis: UFC, WWE workers speak out as safety fears escalate — 'Everyone just can't believe this'
articles.summary: TKO employees say they're being forced to make an impossible choice: Travel to Saudi Arabia amid an escalating military conflict, or risk losing their liveli...
articles.body:
The parent company of the WWE and UFC continues to plow forward with events in Saudi Arabia despite the ongoing military conflict there, but not all those within the company are happy about it.

Sources tell Uncrowned that many people employed by TKO Group Holdings, Inc. are increasingly frustrated at the company's insistence on going through with events in Riyadh, the capital city of Saudi Arabia, even as the country continues to suffer ongoing missile and drone attacks by the Houthi militia in Yemen.

One such attack took place in Riyadh's financial district just hours after WWE's Crown Jewel event concluded nearby on Saturday. While all WWE wrestlers were said to have left the country by the time a missile struck a tower owned by the state-run Aramco oil company on Sunday , some TKO workers said they felt that their safety has been little more than an afterthought as these events have gone on.

"Why are you still even having these shows at this point?" said one source within the company who spoke on the condition of anonymity due to fear of reprisal. "I think the answer is, if they chose not to do the show, they would lose out on millions and millions of dollars.

"From what I've heard, if we don't do the shows in Saudi Arabia or [United Arab Emirate] or Doha or wherever we are going, then our fourth quarter earnings will be off and our shareholders aren't going to get their money," the source continued. "So it's all about greed. They don't care about anybody's well-being. The level of greed with this company is so gross."

Uncrowned reached out to TKO representatives for comment regarding the safety concerns expressed by employees in this story and the company's decision to proceed with events in Saudi Arabia. TKO had not responded at the time of publication.

Multiple events under the TKO banner have been slated for Saudi Arabia this fall, despite the intensifying conflict on both sides of Saudi Arabia's border with Yemen. After attacks ramped up throughout the month of October — including a cruise missile strike on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Oct. 10, which killed 13 people and wounded over 300 more — the U.S. State Department ordered all diplomats and non-emergency government personnel to leave Saudi Arabia , citing security concerns.

Other sports events set to take place in the country, including the Six Kings Slam tennis tournament and the PIF Saudi International golf tournament, have been postponed in light of the attacks.

Fight sports, however, have continued ahead as planned. One prominent recent example was boxer Saul "Canelo" Alvarez's title bout with Christian Mbili on Oct. 31 . That fight took place in Riyadh despite a "hostile aerial threat" warning issued by the Saudi Arabian government just two days prior to the event. The bout was promoted in part by Turki Alalshikh, chairman of Saudi Arabia's General Entertainment Authority. Alalshikh is also a co-founder of Zuffa Boxing, another brand under the TKO banner. Zuffa Boxing has an event planned for Riyadh this Saturday, Nov. 14.

"All [TKO executives] talk about is if the State Department says it is OK to fly there," a source inside the company told Uncrowned. "The rest of us are like, 'If the State Department has to think about it at all, let's just postpone.' That's what all the other sports are doing. Why can't TKO?"

In the weeks leading up to WWE's Crown Jewel event, TKO CEO Ari Emanuel told FOX News that the company was monitoring the situation closely , but felt it was safe to proceed.

"Right now, everything is still set [for WWE Crown Jewel]," Emanuel said on Oct. 23. "This weekend coming up in Abu Dhabi, we have a UFC fight. We have, in the middle of November, a Frieze art show. So, so far, so good — nothing's been cancelled.

"We have a whole team kind of working on this, and kind of when — and if that doesn't happen, where we can move it. It's a daily monitoring."

But ahead of a UFC Fight Night event planned for Riyadh on Dec. 5, some TKO employees say they're increasingly upset by what they see as a disregard for worker safety and a lack of communication about potential contingency plans.

"Not one email has gone out saying, 'Here are the details and the plans for December 5th.' That's crazy," said one source. "They don't tell you anything. They just throw it at you. How about a backup plan? How about a safety letter? 'Hey, if x happens, we go do y. We'll all meet here. We'll do this. We'll do that.' Nothing."

Saturday's WWE event in Saudi Arabia coincided with a Power Slap event in Riyadh on Nov. 6, which some members of the TKO production crew were also expected to work, according to sources. Crews who travel in for WWE or UFC events are routinely asked to work other events for properties like Power Slap or Zuffa Boxing, one source said, with little consideration for the long hours and extra labor involved.

Now, with added concerns amid the ongoing military conflict, some within the company say executive leadership isn't taking their safety seriously enough.

"They don't f***ing care about you one bit," one source said. "People are just getting tired of the way they're getting treated. They get treated like s*** and everybody's tired of it. The lack of communication, the greed, the lack of appreciation, people are just sick of it."

The events in Saudi Arabia, and the risks inherent in traveling to and working from what is essentially an active conflict zone, have pushed some workers to their breaking point, sources say. One longtime TKO employee said the mood among staff darkened after the company refused to move or postpone events even after the airport attacks in the country.

"I'm not the only one who does not want to fly there," one source said, speaking on the condition of anonymity. "It's crazy."

The UFC has moved events under duress in the past, even on extremely short notice. In 2018, following a drug-testing issue involving former champion Jon Jones, the UFC moved an entire event from Las Vegas to California on a few days' notice the week of Christmas.

But when it comes to this series of events scheduled for Saudi Arabia, where site fees have been particularly lucrative for TKO, company leadership has been adamant about proceeding.

In a recent company town hall meeting , TKO President and Chief Operating Officer Mark Shapiro assured employees that the company would "not hesitate" to cancel or postpone events in the region in the face of "danger or a further escalation" in the military conflict. But Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia are now a "near-daily" occurrence in Saudi Arabia, according to The New York Times , and some workers under the TKO banner say the communication from top executives has been lacking.

In his company town hall remarks, Shapiro acknowledged that canceling the events in the region would impact business in "a very negative way," but said that "business is secondary" to employee safety. However, he added that TKO is currently on track for an excellent year financially, which is reflected in a third-quarter earnings report that included an increased targeted revenue of $5.83 billion for the year.

"We want to have the year we all envisioned," Shapiro said in the company town hall. "We've all worked so hard for that year. [20]26 is shaping up to be that year."

As of now, the company has not announced plans to move or postpone any events in Saudi Arabia. With a Zuffa Boxing event on Nov. 14 and a UFC Fight Night event on Dec. 5 looming, and attacks on Riyadh seemingly only ramping up, one source said that there are those in the company considering sitting this one out.

"Everyone is talking about the Middle East shows," the source said on the condition of anonymity. "Who has to go, who can get out of going. Some people say they are waiting until the time to fly comes and telling [executives] that they won't go. But I don't know how many will follow through with that. This is a company that can fire you for no reason or any reason. Everyone just can't believe this is a choice that they are being forced to make — fly into a war zone or risk getting fired before Christmas."

Other workers say they are frustrated, yet more or less resigned to the current state of affairs. Former and current employees described a company culture at TKO that is myopically focused on maximizing short-term profitability, with little regard for the workers who keep the machine running.

"We've come to the realization, this is what it is," one source said. "We're going to either have to accept it or leave, because nothing's going to change at this point. But it's time to get called out. People think it's fine and you get taken care of. People realize the fighters get paid s***. I mean, that's obvious. You guys have covered that aspect of it. People know, and the fighters are starting to speak up for themselves, but it doesn't stop with them. That's the message I want to get across. Everyone across the whole company gets treated like s***, whether you're a fighter or a camera guy."

articles.title: Youth Olympics: Ambekar, Gunjan storm into boxing semifinals, assure India of two medals
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's boxing campaign at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games received a major boost on Tuesday as Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei and Gunjan
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's boxing campaign at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games received a major boost on Tuesday as Lairenlakpam Ambekar Meetei and Gunjan stormed into the semifinals of their respective categories, assuring the country of two medals.Ambekar delivered a commanding performance in the men's 50kg quarterfinal, stopping Namibia's Abraham Kalenga through a Referee Stops Contest (RSC) in the opening round. The bout was stopped at 1 minute and 57 seconds, with the Indian securing his place in the last four without allowing the contest to go the distance.Gunjan followed it up with an equally impressive performance in the women's 48kg category, defeating Mexico's Atena Sofia Juarez Calero 5-0 in her quarterfinal bout. The unanimous decision took her into the semifinals and confirmed India's second boxing medal at the Games.With both boxers advancing to the medal rounds, India are now assured of at least two bronze medals in the competition.Ambekar faces Colombian opponent in semisAmbekar's emphatic victory underlined his dominance in the quarterfinal, as he wrapped up the contest inside the opening two minutes. The Indian will now face Colombia's Izzon Jeffrey Arevalo in the men's 50kg semifinal on Wednesday, with a place in the gold-medal bout at stake.The young boxer will look to carry the momentum from his quarterfinal performance into the last-four clash as he attempts to move closer to the top of the podium.Gunjan, meanwhile, will also be aiming to build on her comprehensive 5-0 victory over Juarez Calero when she steps into the ring for her semifinal bout. Her controlled display ensured that India added another medal to its boxing tally.India look to improve Youth Olympics recordThe two boxing medals add to India's campaign at the fourth edition of the Youth Olympic Games, being held in Dakar, Senegal. The event is a landmark for African sport, with Dakar becoming the first African city to host an Olympic sporting event.The Indian contingent have already won eight medals so far in Dakar: three silver and five bronze medals.India's most successful campaign came at Buenos Aires 2018, where the contingent won 13 medals, including three gold, nine silver and one bronze.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Fury vs AJ undercard: Jai Opetaia could become a global star with spectacular Deontay Wilder win, says Dana White
articles.summary: Jai Opetaia steps up to heavyweight for a bout against hard-punching former champion Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11; "If he wins this fight spectacularly, everything is open and available to Jai Opetaia," promoter Dana White says
articles.body:
Opetaia, an elite cruiserweight, is stepping up to heavyweight for what could be a one-off bout in the division against the former world champion.

Wilder, who previously held the WBC heavyweight title, had a spectacular championship run that earned him the reputation as one of the hardest punchers the sport has ever seen.

Opetaia is already a force in the cruiserweight division and has continued to impressed.

But a victory over Wilder, especially if he wins in style, would take the Australian to a new level of fame.

"Imagine if on this Netflix card Opetaia knocks him out or wins this fight spectacularly, everything is open and available to Jai Opetaia," promoter Dana White told Sky Sports .

"He's one of these unique people who basically has an entire country behind him. He's got Australia and New Zealand. The more he wins, the higher profile fights he has, the bigger he becomes, not just there but all over the world. Everybody knows who Jai Opetaia is now."

Opetaia wants to remain active. "He's willing to fight all the time," White said. "That's the way you stay relevant, forget about making more money and all the stuff that's common sense, that's how you become a legend.

"We're sitting here and talking about Ray Robinson [boxing so frequently] and he did that. That's how you become a legend. Jai is one of those guys."

Oleksandr Usyk, an unbeaten undisputed champion at both heavyweight and cruiserweight, potentially returning to 200lbs creates a new dynamic for the division.

"There's a chance of working with everybody," White hinted, adding: "What does that tell you? It tells that that's the money division right now and Jai Opetaia is a part of it."

Zuffa Boxing's 21-year-old heavyweight Da'Mazion Vanhouter dazzled again on Saturday when he took out Ivan Balaz with stunning speed.

White wants to keep Vanhouter busy and have him box in a month's time on the Fury-AJ undercard too.

"Is this kid the next great American heavyweight? And the answer seems to be yes right now," White said.

"He's another one turning around and fighting again quickly and I believe that [after Balaz] he'll probably be on the Cardiff card too.

"The truth of the matter is why would you not want to be on that card? That's the card you want to be on, especially if you're a heavyweight."

Watch Carlos Adames vs Gerome Warburton from 4pm live on Sky Sports Mix on Saturday.

articles.title: Jake Paul v Cedric Doumbe: 'Crazy I'll get to knock my boss out,' says Doumbe
articles.summary: Cedric Doumbe says it is "crazy" he will get the chance to "face my boss and knock him out" when he fights Jake Paul in Dubai on 24 December.
articles.body:
Cedric Doumbe says it is "crazy" he will get the chance to "face my boss and knock him out" when he fights Jake Paul in Dubai on 24 December.

Doumbe is signed to the Professional Fighters League (PFL) - an MMA organisation that Paul's Most Valuable Promotions merged with in July.

The pair will fight on Christmas Eve in Paul's first bout since being stopped by former world heavyweight champion Anthony Joshua last December.

In a news conference in Paris to promote the event, Cameroonian-born Frenchman Doumbe thanked MVP co-founder Nakisa Bidarian for his role in setting up the fight against Paul.

"I want to thank Nakisa. He's the boss. And Jake, he's the boss, too. I want to thank Nakisa, because that's the first time I will face my boss and knock him out," said Doumbe.

"My boss will pay me to knock him out. That's crazy. We never see that before."

The fight against 29-year-old American Paul is a professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight boxing bout with the fighters using 10oz gloves.

Paul, who is a social media influencer turned professional fighter, has won 12 of his 14 fights as a professional, with his two defeats coming against Tommy Fury and Joshua.

Doumbe, 34, is a former kickboxing world champion who has won two of his three fights since joining the PFL in 2023.

Despite having just one professional boxing bout to his name, which he won in 2015, Doumbe says he's "watching videos on Netflix" instead of training for the fight because he regards Paul as a "joke".

"I do nothing. I just watch videos on Netflix. I just want this fight, this clown fight. I have everything to beat this guy," said Doumbe.

"This guy is a joke. He's a very great YouTuber, but he's not a fighter. He's not even a good boxer. I just need to lose weight to face this guy, that's why I'm training now."

Paul had to have two titanium plates fitted and some teeth removed after having his jaw broken by Joshua - an injury which left his career in doubt.

Last week Paul said on social media he would retire if he lost to Doumbe, before confirming his plans in the news conference.

"I'm 100% retiring if I lose to this guy. For sure," said Paul.

"He's never been in there with someone like me in boxing. It's a completely different sport, that's what he doesn't understand.

"I know he's going to bring a tough fight, but it's just not going to be enough, and that's it at the end of the day."

articles.title: Cedric Doumbe says he 'only needs one punch' to inflict KO loss on Jake Paul in Christmas Eve showdown in Dubai
articles.summary: Cedric Doumbe has insisted he will "only need one punch" to defeat Jake Paul; Doumbe, a two-time world champion kickboxer, will fight Paul on Christmas Eve in Dubai on a Most Valuable Promotions bill; Paul is returning to the ring after his stoppage loss to Anthony Joshua last December
articles.body:
The 29-year-old Paul will face French MMA star Doumbe on December 24 in Dubai, with his promotional company, Most Valuable Promotions (MVP) billing the contest as a "professionally sanctioned eight-round cruiserweight bout".

Doumbe, a former two-time Glory welterweight kickboxing champion, boasts an impressive 75-7-1 record in kickboxing, including 45 knockouts. He is also 6-1 in mixed martial arts and 1-0 as a professional boxer, having beaten Mohamed Fodil on points in his sole boxing appearance back in 2015.

"I just need one punch," Doumbe told a press conference. "I did it 45 times before. One punch. Only one punch.

"You have eight rounds. I only need one punch. And he thinks he will avoid every punch? That's impossible.

"[Paul's] boxing [is his weakness]. He got only three punches. Jab. Right hook. And body jab. That's it. No power. Nothing.

"He's fat. No abs. Nothing. Only good tattoos. But tattoos don't help you in the ring."

Paul dropped out of the WBA cruiserweight rankings following his sixth-round stoppage defeat to Anthony Joshua in Miami last December. The loss also cast doubt over his boxing future, with the American requiring surgery to repair his jaw.

Asked about his recovery, Paul insisted he was ready to return, revealing that his jaw had been reinforced with titanium.

"Titanium. Stronger than ever. We're ready for this guy. Kickboxing world champion, Glory champion, one of the best in MMA, this guy is great, he is great. But he's getting knocked out on Christmas Eve," Paul said.

articles.summary: Dana White's Power Slap sent a cease and desist to the Lingerie Fighting Championships over its butt-slapping parody event called Power Spank.
articles.body: Can we live in a world where both slapping and spanking combat sports exist? I'd like to believe so. articles.title: El clan Nurmagomedov ataca por la espalda a Merab Dvalishvili, amigo íntimo de Topuria, y el 'Matador' estalla
articles.standfirst: Ha ocurrido este miércoles en Abu Dhabi
articles.summary: Ha ocurrido este miércoles en Abu Dhabi
articles.body: La tarde del miércoles sorprendió a todos cuando, desde Abu Dhabi, Merab Dvalishvili, ex campeón del peso gallo de UFC y amigo íntimo de Ilia y Aleksandre Topuria, denunciaba en sus redes sociales, con el rostro lleno de sangre, que había sufrido una emboscada por parte de Usman Nurmagomedov (campeón de PFL, posible futuro fichaje de UFC y primo de Khabib), Umar Nurmagomedov (hermano de Usman y ex rival de Merab por el título) y un grupo de más de 10 peleadores del Daguestán. "Son unos cobardes, unos cobardes. Nos atacaron por la espalda. Eso no lo hace un hombre de verdad", denunció Merab. Minutos después, Ilia Topuria lanzaba un mensaje en redes sociales en defensa del georgiano. "Sois un puñado de cobardes y tendréis que rendir cuentas por lo que habéis hecho. Sois todo menos hombres de verdad", tuiteaba el hispanogeorgiano en un mensaje que después borraría. El post, además, estaba acompañado de un vídeo en el que se veía el momento del ataque... justo mientras entrevistaban a Merab en el hotel de los peleadores de Abu Dhabi. Merab se encuentra en Emiratos Árabes Unidos para participar este fin de semana en una nueva velada de RAF Wrestling, una compañía de lucha que tiene muchos peleadores de UFC en nónima. Umar Nurmagomedov también está entre los participantes, aunque no se iba a medir a Merab.
